docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This is a testing website for the juvix-mkdocs plugin, a MkDocs plugin that can render Juvix code blocks in Markdown files, generating Isabelle theories from Juvix Markdown files, all this with support for snippets and wiki links.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
To install it, run:

pip3 install mkdocs-juvix-plugin

If you already have a project, add the plugin and add the following to your mkdocs.yml file:

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
  - juvix
  # - todos

Front-matter options can be added to any file to customize the behavior of the plugin. For example, to generate Isabelle theories from Juvix Markdown files, add the following to the front-matter of the file:

---
preprocess:
  juvix: true
  isabelle: true
  isabelle_at_bottom: true
---

For more information, here are some tutorials:

  • Juvix Markdown file structure
  • Generate Isabelle theories for inclusion in the documentation
  • Snippet support for inclusion of content from external files
  • Support for Wiki Links
  • Bibliography support
  • To-do Plugin
  • Diagrams using Kroki

docs.title: Everything
docs.text:
This is file is not mandatory to be included in the documentation. However, it can be useful to test the compilation of the documentation with all the features enabled.

module everything;import test;import isabelle;import diagrams;

docs.title: Support for including images
docs.text:
Images should be stored in the docs/images folder.

Image handling in Markdown

Use standard Markdown image syntax (![Alt text](image.png)) rather than HTML image tags. HTML image tags are not processed by MkDocs, are not validated, and may not work as expected. In particular, their src attribute is not processed by our image processing script.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
To add an image, apply the following syntax:

![Alt Text](logo.svg){: width="200"}

docs.title: Displayed Image Example
docs.text:
The syntax above will render the image in your document like so:

Enhanced Image Display

Use an HTML <figure> element with a <figcaption> for a refined presentation with captions. Markdown can also be used within the caption:

<figure markdown="1">

  ![Alt Text](image-name.png)

  <figcaption markdown="span">Image caption text can include *Markdown*!</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: Juvix can be used to generate Isabelle theories
docs.text:
For example, we can define the following Juvix module, assuming the file is named isabelle.juvix:

module isabelle;type Nat : Type :=  | zero  | succ Nat;add : Nat -> Nat -> Nat  | zero n := n  | (succ m) n := succ (add m n);

And then we can generate an Isabelle theory from it with the following command:

juvix isabelle isabelle.juvix

This will generate a file isabelle.thy in the current directory.

Isabelle/HOL theories generated for this page

docs.title: Isabelle/HOL theories
docs.text:
isabelle.thy
theory isabelle
imports Main
begin

datatype Nat
  = zero |
    succ Nat

(* --8<-- [start:isabelle-add-def] *)
fun add :: "Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat" where
  "add zero n = n" |
  "add (succ m) n = (succ (add m n))"
(* --8<-- [end:isabelle-add-def] *)
end

docs.title: Test
docs.text:
This is a test file.

This is the first Juvix code block:

module test;import Stdlib.Prelude open;

And this is the second Juvix code block:

main : String := "Hello world!";

docs.title: Bibliography Support
docs.text:
Enable bibliography support in mkdocs.yml:

plugins:
  - bibtex:
      bib_dir: "docs/references"

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Place .bib files in docs/references
  2. New .bib files are automatically processed

docs.text:
Cite references using: 

This statement requires a citation [@citation_key].

docs.title: Diagrams using Kroki
docs.text:
Enable Kroki support in mkdocs.yml:

plugins:
  - kroki:
      ServerURL: !ENV [KROKI_SERVER_URL, 'https://kroki.io']
      FileTypes:
        - png
        - svg
      FileTypeOverrides:
        mermaid: png

See the Diagrams using Kroki page for examples.

docs.title: Quick Installation
docs.text:
To install the juvix-mkdocs plugin, run:

pip3 install mkdocs-juvix-plugin

Add the plugin to your mkdocs.yml:

mkdocs.yml
plugins:
  - juvix
  # - todos

docs.title: Front-matter Options
docs.text:
Customize plugin behavior using front-matter options:

---
preprocess:
  juvix: true
  isabelle: true
  include_at_bottom: true
---

docs.title: Creating a New Project
docs.text:
Create a new project using the CLI command:

juvix-mkdocs new my-juvix-project

View all options with:

juvix-mkdocs new --help

For Anoma setup:

juvix-mkdocs new my-juvix-project --anoma-setup

docs.title: Building and Running
docs.text:
Build the website: 

juvix-mkdocs build

Run the development server: 

juvix-mkdocs serve

Some flags are available for these commands:

  • --remove-cache: Remove the cache database.
  • --verbose: Print verbose output.
  • --debug: Print debug output.
  • --no-open: Do not open the browser after building.
  • --quiet: Do not print any output.

Development Mode

For development, after poetry install and poetry shell: 

juvix-mkdocs new -n -f -D
juvix-mkdocs serve -p my-juvix-project

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Enable Isabelle theory generation in front-matter:

---
preprocess:
  isabelle: true
---

To include theories at page bottom:

---
preprocess:
  isabelle: true
  isabelle_at_bottom: true
---

docs.title: Including Generated Files
docs.text:
Include the generated Isabelle theory as a snippet using the !thy suffix:

--8<-- "docs/isabelle.juvix.md!thy:isabelle-add-def"

This provides the following output:

isabelle.thy from isabelle.juvix.md
fun add :: "Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat" where
  "add zero n = n" |
  "add (succ m) n = (succ (add m n))"

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
A Juvix Markdown file (.juvix.md) must follow these rules:

  • The first Juvix code block must declare a module matching the file name
  • Code blocks must contain well-defined Juvix expressions
  • Module names must follow folder structure

Example: tutorial/basics.juvix.md

module tutorial.basics;
-- ...

docs.title: Code Block Features
docs.text:
Enable Juvix code blocks in mkdocs.yml: 

plugins:
  - juvix

docs.title: Hiding Code Blocks
docs.text:
Hide code blocks using the hide attribute:

````juvix hide
module tutorial.basics;
-- ...
```

docs.title: Extracting Module Statements
docs.text:
Extract inner module statements:

````juvix extract-module-statements
module B;
module C;
-- ...
```

With a specific number of statements:

````juvix extract-module-statements 2
module B;
axiom a : Nat;
module C;
-- ...
```

docs.title: Disabling Processing
docs.text:
Disable Juvix processing per file: 

---
preprocess:
  juvix: false
---

docs.title: Snippet Support
docs.text:
To incorporate the excerpt elsewhere, specify its path and tag:

--8<-- "path/to/file.ext:TAG"

docs.title: Snippets of Juvix code
docs.text:
You can also include snippets of Juvix code in your Markdown files. This is done by adding the --8<-- comment followed by the path to the file, and optionally a snippet identifier.

The following example shows how to include a snippet of Juvix code from the file test.juvix.md with the identifier main.

--8<-- "docs/test.juvix.md:main"

which provides the following output:

main : String := "Hello world!";

You can also include relative paths:

axiom A : Type;

Info

If the path of the file ends with !, the raw content of the file will be included. Otherwise, for Juvix Markdown files, the content will be preprocessed by the Juvix compiler and then the generated HTML will be included.

So if we would like to include the raw content of test.juvix.md, we can do this by specifying the path as docs/test.juvix.md!:main.

main : String := "Hello world!";

Snippet identifier

To use a snippet identifier, you must wrap the Juvix code block with the syntax <!-- --8<-- [start:snippet_identifier] --> and <!-- --8<-- [end:snippet_identifier] -->. This technique is useful for including specific sections of a file. Alternatively, you use the standard --8<-- markers within the code and extract the snippet by appending a ! at the end of the path.

docs.title: Snippet for generated Isabelle files
docs.text:
For including generated Isabelle files, the path of the file must end with !thy, the raw content of the Isabelle theory file will be included.

--8<-- "docs/isabelle.juvix.md!thy:isabelle-add-def"

This provides the following output:

isabelle.thy from isabelle.juvix.md
fun add :: "Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat \<Rightarrow> Nat" where
  "add zero n = n" |
  "add (succ m) n = (succ (add m n))"

docs.title: Todos Plugin
docs.text:
Enable the todos plugin in mkdocs.yml:

plugins:
  - todos

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Create todos using:

!!! todo

    Content of the todo

This renders as:

Todo

Content of the todo

Info

Todos are removed from online versions by default. Set todos: True in front-matter to keep them.

docs.title: Wiki Links Support
docs.text: Wiki links offer a simple method for citing and referencing other pages in the documentation without lengthy URLs. Wiki links are the preferred method for linking to other pages in the documentation, so please use them whenever possible.

docs.title: Basic Syntax
docs.text:
The basic syntax for a wiki link is:

page

Where:

  • page is the title of the target page

docs.title: Full Syntax
docs.text:
The full syntax for a wiki link is: Wiki Link Syntax

  Custom caption

When resolving a wiki link, the system follows these rules:

docs.title: Page Title
docs.text:
(Mandatory) The 'page' in a wiki link refers to the title specified in the nav attribute of the mkdocs.yml file. For example,

mkdocs.yml
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - MyRef X: reference.md

provides the following wiki link:

MyRef X

docs.title: Path Hints
docs.text:
(Optional) You can use path hints to specify the location of the file. The syntax is:

Path Hints
page

Where:

  • hintpath/to is the path (or prefix) to the file
  • page is the title of the target page

docs.title: Anchors
docs.text:
(Optional) Use anchors to link to specific sections within a page. If the page does not have an anchor, the link would render as the caption provided, and you'll find a warning in the build process.

Anchors
page

Where:

  • page is the title of the target page
  • anchor is a specific section within the page

docs.title: Custom captions
docs.text:
(Optional) Provide custom text to display for the link instead of the page title.

Custom Captions
Custom caption

Where:

  • page is the title of the target page
  • anchor is a specific section within the page

Captions can include icons, for example:

MarkdownPreview 
:material-link: this is a caption with an icon

this is a caption with an icon

docs.title: List of wiki-style links per Page
docs.text:
By default, the build process will generate a list of all wiki-style links per page. This list is displayed at the bottom of the page, and it is useful for identifying broken links or pages that are not linked to from other pages.

To disable this feature, set the list_wikilinks option to false in the front matter of the page.

Front-matter of a page
---
list_wikilinks: false
---
